translations.text: And it came to pass in the month of Chislev, in the twentieth year of King Artaxerxes, that I was in Susa, among the capital cities of Abira.
And one of my brothers came, and men of Judah. And I asked them about those who had been saved and had escaped from the captivity, and about Jerusalem.

And he said to me: "Those who escaped from their captivity are there, in their own land, in great distress and reproach. And the walls of Jerusalem are still broken down and destroyed, and its gates have been burned with fire."
And it came to pass, when I heard these words, that I sat down and wept and mourned for many days, and I fasted and worshipped before the Lord, my God of heaven.
And I said: "O Lord God of heaven and earth, you who are mighty and great and terrible, keep your covenant and mercy for those who love you and who have kept your law.

Let your ears be open to hear and your eyes to see. And now hear and see the prayer of your servant, which we offer before you today for the sons of Israel, your servants, who have been given over to affliction because of our sins, which we have sinned against you. I and my father's house have sinned.
And we have utterly transgressed, and have not kept your law and your commandments and your judgements, which you commanded us by the hand of your servant Moses.
Remember, O Lord, the word that you commanded Moses your servant: 'If you do not keep my law, I will scatter you among the nations.'

'If you return and keep my law and do them, then even if you are scattered to the end of the earth, from there I will gather you and bring you to the place that I have chosen, where my name dwells upon it.'
And now, behold, your servants and your people, whom you redeemed by your might and by your great power and by your high arm —

do not cast us away from your hands, but let your ears be attentive to the prayer of your servant, and hear the supplication of those who fear your name, O Lord. And prosper this petition of your servants before you today. And grant me to find mercy before this man." And I was the king's cupbearer.

And it came to pass in the month of Nisan, in the twentieth year of King Artaxerxes, that he asked me for wine. And I took the wine and gave it to the king to drink. And the king was alone when he drank the wine.
The king said to me: "Why is your face sad, and what is the cause of it, if not wickedness?" And I was very much afraid.

And I said to the king: "O king, live forever! Why should my face not be grieved and sad, since that city, the house of our fathers, is a desert, and its gates have been destroyed by fire without mercy?"
And the king said to me: "For what matter are you asking this?" And I prayed to the Lord, the God of heaven.

And I said to the king: "May good be upon your kingdom! And if I, your servant, have found favour before your face, and you are willing to send me to Judea, to the city of the memorial of our fathers, then by your word I will rebuild that city of God."

And the king said to me, and his concubine who was sitting with him: "How long until you are finished, or when will you return from there?" And the king did good to me and sent me off, and I set him a time.
And I said to the king: "If I have found favour before you, give me letters to the governors of the region beyond the river, so that they may escort me until I reach Judea.

And a letter to Asaph, who is the keeper of the royal garden, so that he may give me timber to build the gates and the walls, and for the city, and for the house that I shall enter there." And the king gave it to me, for the hand of my God was with me for good.
And I came to the governors of the region of the river and gave them the king's letters. And the king sent mighty commanders with me, and letters and horses.
And Sanballat the governor and Tobiah, the servant of Ammon, heard of it, and it seemed evil to them, because men were seeking me out in goodwill, to help Israel [?].
And we came to Jerusalem and stayed there only three days.

And I rose at night, I and a few men who were with me. And I did not tell the men what God had put into my heart to do for Israel. And there was no beast with me except the one beast on which I was riding.

And I went out by the Ravine Gate, facing the land of the fig trees, and as far as the Gate of the Springs. And I was distressed by how narrow the passage was along the wall of Jerusalem, which they had cleared [?]. And its gates had been destroyed by fire.

And I passed by the Gate of the Spring, beside the outflows of the waters. These are the Ammonites and Moabites and Samaritans of the king [?]. And there was no room there for my beast to let me pass that place on horseback.
And at night I went up on the wall on the ravine side, and I was distressed by the narrowness on the wall. And I came to the Valley Gate and turned back.

And the watchmen did not notice where I had gone or what I was doing. And until then I had not told the Jews, or the priests, or the nobles, or the officials, or the others who carried out the labour of the work.

And I said to them: "You see this misfortune that we are now in, how Jerusalem is desolate and its gates are burned with fire. Come, let us rebuild the walls of Jerusalem, so that we will no longer be a reproach."

And I told them that the hand of the Lord had been upon me for good, and I told them the words that the king had spoken to me. And I said to them: "Now come, let us rise up and work, and let us build this place of God." And their hands were strengthened for the good work.

And Sanballat heard of it, along with Ahron [?] and Tobiah, servants of Ammon, and Geshem the Arabian. And they mocked us, and came to us and said to us: "What is this thing that you are doing? Do you want to rebel against the king?"

And I answered and said to them: "The God of heaven has prospered us, and we are his holy servants. And we will build this city of God. But you have no portion, no memorial and no right in Jerusalem."

Eliashib the high priest rose up, together with his brothers the priests, and they built the gate of the pools of the Cave [?]. And they sanctified it, and set up the gates of the Cave, and built it as far as the tower of Hananel.
And at the hands of the men of Jericho, and at the hands of the sons of Zaccur, the sons of Amari.
And the sons of Hassenaah built the gate on the far side [?]. And they laid its beams [?] and set up its locks and its bolts.
Beside them Meremoth held [the work], along with the sons of Koreis, of Akoth. Beside them Meshullam son of Baruch, son of Ieses, Zebel [?] held. And beside them Zadok son of Baana held.
Next to them Tekuim and Adurev held. They did not give their necks to their service.
Joiada son of Phaleb and Meshullam son of Baneah held the Old Gate. They set it in order and set up its doors, its bars and its bolts.
After their arrangement of this, Hananiah son of Hrook held [the work], and he left [the rest of] Jerusalem as far as the wall of the square.
After them Rephaiah, the ruler of the districts of Jerusalem, held [the work].
Beside him Jedaiah son of Erosaph held [the work], on the side of his own house. Beside him Hattush son of Asban held [the work].
Malchijah son of Aram, and Hasshub son of Pahath-moab, held a second [section], as far as the Tower of the Ovens.
Beside him Shallum son of Hallohesh, the ruler of half of the Jerusalem district, held [the work], along with his daughters.
Hanun and those who live in Zanoah held the Valley Gate. They built it and set up its doors, its bars and its bolts. They also built a thousand cubits of its wall as far as the Ash Gate.
Malchijah son of Rechab, the ruler of the districts of Beth-haccherem, held the Ash Gate. He himself and [the people of] his districts covered [?] it and set up its doors, its locks and its bolts.
Ordion, the king's official, held the wall of the water channels of the springs, as far as the ascent that goes down from the City of David.
After him Nehemiah son of Azbuk, the ruler of Beth-zur, held [the work] as far as the Garden of David, to the water outflows that had been made, and as far as Beth-haggibborim.
After him the Levites held [the work]: Rehum son of Baneah. Beside him Hashabiah, the ruler of the Keilah district, held [the work].
After this his sons held [the work]: Benaiah son of Adad, the ruler of the Keilah district.
After him Asur son of Iakus, the ruler of Mizpah, held part of the second wall, which went up next to the corner of the tower.
After him Baruch son of Zabun held a second section, from the corner as far as the gate of Beth-Eliashib, where the high priest stands.
After him Meremoth son of Uriah, son of Hakkoz, held a second section, from the gate of Gethelyasob [?] to its end.
After him the priests, the men of Akhekham [?], held [the work].
After him Benjamin and Hasshub held [the work] in front of their houses. After him Azariah son of Maaseiah, son of Ananiah, held [the work] near his house.
After him Binnui son of Henadad held a second section, from Beth-azariah as far as the corner and the turn of the ascent of that place.
Palal son of Uzziah held [the work] opposite the dwelling [?] and the tower that stood outside the royal palaces, above the prison court. After him Pedaiah son of Parosh held [the work].
And the temple servants [Nethinim], who lived in Ophel, on the garden road [?], at the gate on the side of the springs, toward the east, and the outer tower.
After him the men of Tekoa repaired a second section, opposite the great tower that stood outside, as far as the wall of the village [?Ophel].
Above the Horse Gate the priests repaired, each man opposite his own house.
After him Zadok son of Immer repaired opposite his own house. After him Shemaiah son of Shecaniah, the keeper of the East Gate, repaired.
After him Hananiah son of Shelemiah and Hanun son of Zalaph repaired a second section. After him Meshullam son of Berechiah repaired opposite the house of his treasure.
After him Malchijah son of Zarephath repaired as far as Beth-hanathim, along with the other rich men of the city, and opposite the Miphkad Gate as far as the exit of the corner.
At the middle gate of the water outlets the coppersmiths [?] and the rich men of the city repaired.
When Sanballat heard that we were building the walls and raising up its walls, it grieved him. He became very angry and mocked Judea.
He said before his brothers: "Is this your strength, O Samaritans? How are these Jews building and fortifying their cities?"

Tobiah the Ammonite had come to them, and he said to them: "How could they ever manage to build, or to offer sacrifices, or to eat of the offerings in that place of theirs? Will foxes not go up there and break down the stones of its walls?" [?]
Hear us, O Lord our God, for we have become an object of mockery and contempt. Turn their insults back on their own heads, and give them up to be mocked before those who take them captive.
Do not cover up their iniquities.

When Sanballat and Tobiah, and the Arabians and the Ammonites, heard that the building of the walls of Jerusalem had gone well, and that we had begun, each in his own place, to bring the work to light [?], it seemed evil to them.
They all gathered together to come and fight against Jerusalem.
We prayed to the Lord our God, and because of the enemy we set guards over ourselves day and night.
The men of Judea said: "We cannot fight and build like this. Instead, let some stand ready and armed, and let others build."
Those who were oppressing us said: "We will not let them know until we rise up, each from our own place, and come among them, slaughter them, and stop their work."
Then the Jews who lived in various places came and said to us: "They may come out against us from every place."
So we stationed people in the lower places behind the wall, beneath the upper storey, and we set armed men there: spearmen and archers.

I rose and spoke to the men who stood ready and watchful, to their leaders, and to those who were keeping guard in various places: "Do not be afraid of them. Remember the Lord our God, great and terrible, and fight for your brothers, your sons, your wives, and your houses."

And it came to pass, when our enemies heard that we had learned of it and had made ourselves ready and watchful to fight them, God brought their plan to nothing. And all of us went back to building the wall, each man to his own place.

And it came to pass that from that day on some were assigned to the work and some were armed and faced the enemy, with spear and shield and bow in their hands. And they stood ready, each man back to back with his brother.
Those who were building the wall would help their brothers whenever there was occasion. Each held his weapon in one hand and with the other hand passed stone or clay to his brother.
Each of those who were building had his sword girded at his waist and a leg-guard on his leg, and in this way they built the walls of Jerusalem. And those who blew the horn trumpet stood near them.
And I said to the men who were armed and ready, and to their rulers: "This work is great and wide. We are spread out in building this wall, and each of us is far from his brother.
Now let us station men in place after place to blow the trumpets. When you hear the sound of the horn trumpet, all of you gather there. And our God will fight all our enemies for us."
At all times some worked while others held their weapons ready, from the break of dawn until the stars came out. At all times some worked while others held their weapons, from morning until evening.
And I said to the men of the people: "Come, let us stay inside the city of Jerusalem. Let us post guards around us at night and work by day."
And I stood watch with the men around me who guarded me, and none of us took off his clothes or put aside his weapon.
And the people and their wives raised an outcry, man against his brother,
and they said: "Our sons and our daughters lack food. Let us go and buy grain and eat."
And some said: "Let us give our fields, our vineyards and our houses as a pledge, and get wheat and eat."
And some said: "Let us give up our possessions and get gold and silver, and pay it as tribute to the king."

"And now our flesh is like the flesh of our brothers, and our children are like their children. Why, then, have we given up our sons and our daughters? They have been taken away by force, and we have no power in our hands to redeem them. And now our flesh is like the flesh of our brothers, and our children are like their children. Why, then, have we given our sons and our daughters into slavery? They have been taken away by force, and we have no power in our hands to redeem them."
And I was deeply distressed when I heard their outcry and their words.

I thought it over in my mind and began to argue with the nobles and their rulers. I said to them: "You are the ones who exact tribute from your brothers." And I ordered them to gather a great assembly.

And I said to them: "We redeemed our brothers the Jews who had been sold among the gentiles, which we could not understand [?]. And you have sold them!" And they fell silent and could not answer me anything.
And I said: “The thing you are doing is not good, because you do not fear God. Because of this we cannot escape the reproach of the gentiles and of our enemies.”
And I said to my brothers and to those I knew, and I say it to you as well: “Let us give our silver and our produce as ransom, the ransom that those tax collectors demand,
and let us redeem their fields and vineyards and olive groves and houses today with our silver. And let them buy wheat and wine and oil and bring these to them.”

And the rulers and the other great men said: “Let us give them back, and we will take nothing from them. We will do as you have commanded us.” And I called the priests and made them swear to keep this word. And the rulers said: “We will do as you have commanded us.” And I called the priests and made them swear to keep this word.

And I shook out my [?] (the fold of my garment) hard and said: “In the same way may God shake out every man who does not carry out these words, out of his life and out of his place. In the same way may he be shaken out and emptied of his life.” And all the people of the assembly said: “Amen.” And they blessed God. And the whole assembly did as it had promised and carried out this word.

And from the day when I commanded that they should not be rulers over Judah, from the twentieth year to the thirty-second year of King Artaxerxes, for twelve years, I and my brothers were the rulers. We ate no one's food by force, and we drank nothing either.

And those who had oppressed the people before had laid heavy burdens on them and taken their bread and wine and everything else from them. I gave silver didrachmas to their lords and removed these men from ruling over the people. And I was not like them, because of the fear of the Lord.
And the work on the wall went well. I oppressed no one and took nothing from anyone, whether a vineyard or anything else. And all of them worked on the wall without growing weary.
And about a hundred men of the Jews, along with others from the gentiles around us who came to us, I brought in and fed at my own table.

And each day one [?] (perhaps an ox or a calf), six choice sheep and one yearling lamb were prepared for me. This was my daily ration. And every ten days I gave wine freely for them to drink. I took no one's bread or wine by force, because I knew that the work was heavy for the people.
Remember me for good, O Lord, for what I have done for all this people.
And when Sanballat and Tobiah and the land of the Arabians and many others of our enemies heard that we had built the walls, their strength failed them. Only the gates there had not yet been set up.
And Sanballat and Geshem sent word and said to me: “Come, let us meet together in the villages of the plain of Ono.” But they were planning to do me harm.

I sent messengers to them and said to them: “The work that I am doing is a great work. I have no time to come down to you, because I do not want this work to be broken off halfway. When I have finished this work, I will come down to you.”
And they sent to me many times, and each time I gave them the same answer.
And Sanballat sent his servant to me with an unsealed letter in his hand,

In it was written: "All the nations have heard that you and the Jews intend to rebel against the king. That is why you are building those walls and strengthening those towers: you intend to become king.

"That is also why you have appointed prophets, because you intend to take your seat in Jerusalem and reign over Judea. Now this report may well reach the king. So come, and let the two of us discuss it together."
I sent word back to him and said: "Nothing like what you say has happened. You are making it up out of your own head."
Everyone was trying to frighten us, saying: "Their hands will grow slack, and [?] they will [not] finish their work." But now I strengthened my hands, so that this work would be finished completely.

I went into the house of Shemaiah son of Delaiah, son of Mehetabel. He was shut up in his own house, and he said to me: "Let us meet in the house of the Lord, take refuge inside it and lock its doors. Otherwise our enemies may come by night and kill you."
I said: "Who is this man I should run away from? Or what man like me would go into the house of the Lord to save his life?"
I understood that God had not sent him, and that this was no prophet's word for me.
Tobiah and Sanballat had paid many people to work against me so that I would become frightened and go into the house of the Lord. And I knew that it was so that they could give me a bad name.
May the Lord remember me in the face of the treachery of Tobiah and Sanballat. They plotted evil against me and pushed people to prophesy falsely so that he could frighten me and make me tremble.
The wall was finished on the twenty-fifth of the month of Elul. It took fifty-two days.
When all our enemies heard this, all the nations around us trembled. Great dread and fear fell on them, and they understood that our work had been accomplished by God.
In those days the Jews sent letters to Tobiah with great honour, and Tobiah came to them.
They knew one another, and he was the son-in-law of Shecaniah son of Arah. His son Jonathan had married the daughter of Meshullam son of Berechiah.
They kept bringing his words to me and reporting my words to him. He also wrote many letters to frighten me.
Once the wall had been built, I set up its gates, and the gatekeepers, the psalm singers and the Levites were appointed.
I gave orders to Hananiah and to my brothers. Hananiah was ruler over Jerusalem, because he was a faithful man and feared God more than most.

I said to him: "Do not open the gates of Jerusalem early, before the sun has risen. While everyone is still awake, shut the gates and bar them with locks. Post guards from among the inhabitants of Jerusalem, some men at their watch posts and other men each at his own house.
"For this city is large and spacious, but the people in it are few, and not all the houses have been built yet."

Then God put it into my heart to gather the honourable leaders and all the people into a single assembly. I found a book listing the families who had first come up from the captivity, and this is what was written in it:
These are the children who came out of captivity, those whom Nebuchadnezzar king of Babylon had carried off into exile, and who returned to Jerusalem and Judea, each to his own city,
who came with Zerubbabel, and with Jeshua, and with Nehemiah, Azariah, and Elmia, Neemeani, Mordecai, Bilshan, Marasparath, Ezra, Bigvai, Nahum, Baanah, Mispar: the men of the people of Israel:
the sons of Parosh, two thousand and seventy-two;
the sons of Shephatiah, three hundred and seventy-two;
the sons of Arah, six hundred and fifty-two;
the sons of Pahath-moab, of the sons of Jeshua and of Joab, two thousand two hundred and eighteen;
the sons of Elam, one thousand two hundred and sixty-two [literally "fifty and twelve"];
the sons of Zattu, eight hundred and forty-five;
the sons of Zaccai, seven hundred and sixty;
the sons of Bani, six hundred and forty-eight;
the sons of Bebai, six hundred and forty-eight;
the sons of Azgad, two thousand and sixty-two;
the sons of Adonikam, six hundred and forty-four;
the sons of Ater of Hezekiah, ninety-eight;
the sons of Samei [?], three hundred and twenty-eight;
the sons of Beniaz [?], three hundred and twenty-three;
the sons of Gibeon, one hundred and twelve;
the sons of Bethlehem, one hundred and twenty-three; the sons of Netophah, fifty-three;
the sons of Anathoth, one hundred and twenty-eight;
the men of Beth-azmaveth, forty-two;
the men of Kiriath-jearim, Chephirah and Beeroth, eight hundred and forty-three;
the men of Bemakerama [?], one hundred and twenty-two;
the men of Bethel and Ai, one hundred and twenty-three;
the men of Nebo, one hundred and fifty-two; the men of Magbish, one hundred and fifty-six;
the men of Elam, one thousand two hundred and fifty-six;
The sons of Harim, three hundred and twenty;
the sons of Jericho, three hundred and forty-five;
the sons of Lod, Hadid and Ono, seven hundred and forty-three;
the sons of Ananiah, three thousand nine hundred and thirty.
And the priests: the sons of Judah, of the house of Jeshua, nine hundred and sixty-nine;
the sons of Immer, one thousand and fifty-two;
the sons of Pashhur, one thousand two hundred and forty-seven;
the sons of Jeram, one thousand and seventeen [?].
And the Levites: the sons of Jeshua and Kadmiel, of the sons of Hodaviah, seventy-two.
The singers of psalms: the sons of Asaph, one hundred and forty-eight.
The gatekeepers: the sons of Loma [?], the sons of Ater, the sons of Timoen [?], the sons of Akkub, the sons of Hatita, the sons of Sabea, one hundred and thirty-two.
And the kindred of Mael [?]: the sons of Sila, the sons of Asaph, the sons of Tabbaoth,
the sons of Keros, the sons of Sia, the sons of Pharon,
the sons of Laban, the sons of Agabiah, the sons of Akud, the sons of Ota, the sons of Ketar, the sons of Agab, the sons of Selem,
the sons of Anan, the sons of Gader, the sons of Gaar,
the sons of Rei, the sons of Hraason, the sons of Nesoda,
the sons of Beisam, the sons of Oz, the sons of Vesov,
the sons of Gesev, the sons of Meinom, the sons of Phoam,
the sons of Babuk, the sons of Akepha, the sons of Aror, the sons of Babuk, the sons of Akepha, the sons of Aror,
the sons of Basaloth, the sons of Meida, the sons of Adasal, the sons of Basaloth, the sons of Meida, the sons of Adasal,
the sons of Sovea, the sons of Atupha.
The sons of the servants of Solomon: the sons of Sut, the sons of Sapharath, the sons of Pherada,
the sons of Jaale, the sons of Dorkon, the sons of Gadiel,
the sons of Shephatiah, the sons of Etemi, the sons of Phakarat, the sons of Sabaiam, the sons of Liim,
the sons of the Nathaim [?], the sons of the servants of Solomon, three hundred and ninety-two.
These are the ones who came up from Tel-melech: Telara, Cherub, Run and Emer. They could not give the names of their fathers, or tell about their own kindred, whether they were of Israel:
the sons of Delaiah, the sons of Bua, the sons of Tobiah and the sons of Koda, six hundred and forty-two.
And from the priests: the sons of Habaiah, the sons of Hakkoz and the sons of Barzillai. He took a wife from the daughters of Barzillai the Gileadite and was called by his name.
These looked for the record of their kindred and did not find it, and they were excluded from the priesthood.
He said to them, “They must not eat of the holy things of the sanctuary until a priest arises who will clearly enlighten them.”
The whole people of the assembly numbered fourteen myriads, four thousand three hundred and sixty (144,360),
besides their male and female servants, who numbered seven thousand three hundred and thirty-seven. The singers of psalms, men and women, numbered two hundred and forty-five.
They had seven hundred and thirty-six horses and two hundred and forty-five mules,
four hundred and thirty-four camels and four thousand seven hundred and twenty donkeys.
The rulers, the heads of the fathers' houses, gave for the work. Artasasta gave gold worth only a thousand, along with fifty bowls and thirty priestly tunics.
The rulers, the heads of the fathers' houses, gave for the work two myriads (20,000) in gold, a myriad (10,000) in silver, and two thousand two hundred minas.
The rest of the people gave two myriads (20,000) drachmas, about two thousand silver vessels and three thousand and seven priestly tunics.
The chief priests and the Levites, the gatekeepers, the singers of psalms, those of the people, the Nethinim and all Israel settled in their own cities.

The seventh month came, and the children of Israel were in their own cities. All the people gathered as one man in the square in front of the Water Gate. They told Ezra, the scribe of the law, to bring the law of Moses, which the Lord God of Israel had commanded.
Ezra the priest brought the law before the assembly, where men and women had gathered, together with all who wished to hear, on the first day of their seventh month.

He began reading to them at dawn, when the sun rose, and went on until the sixth hour, before the men and women. They all understood, and all the people listened closely to the book of the law of the Lord.

Ezra, the priest and scribe, stood on a wooden platform. Beside him stood Mattithiah and Shema, Anaiah and Uriah, Hilkiah and Maaseiah. On his left were Pedaiah and Mishael, Malchijah and Osiam, Sabna, Zechariah and Meshullam.
Ezra opened the books in front of the whole assembly, because he was set over all the people. When he had opened the books and the people had stood up before him,
Ezra blessed the Lord, the great God, and all the people said, “So be it! So be it!” They raised their hands toward heaven, bowed down and worshipped the Lord God with their faces to the ground.
Jeshua, Bani and Sherebiah helped the people understand the law, and the people stood in their proper order.
They read out the book of the law of God, explaining it and making it clear, so that the people would understand the word and know it.

Nehemiah, who is the governor (Athersatha), and Ezra the priest and scribe of the law, and the Levites who were teaching all the people, said: "This day is holy to the Lord our God. Do not mourn and do not weep." For the people were weeping as they heard the words of the law of the Lord.

They said to them: "Go, eat and drink your rich foods and your sweet things from your stores, and send portions to those who have nothing. For this day is holy to the Lord our God. Now be strong, and do not distress those who are in want."
And the Levites quieted the people, saying to them: "Be quiet and do not be dismayed, for this day is holy."
And the people went away to eat and drink, and they sent portions to those who had none. And they made great rejoicing, because they had understood the words of the law that he had read to them.

On the second day the rulers and the heads of the fathers' houses of all the people, the priests and the Levites, gathered to Ezra the scribe of the law, so that they might gain understanding and learn from him all the words of the law.
And they found written in the law, which had been commanded by the Lord God to Moses, how the children of Israel ought to dwell in the seventh month.

And also how the trumpet should announce it in all the cities and in Jerusalem. And Ezra said: "Go up to the mountain and bring olive branches, and branches of the elm tree, and branches of myrtle for incense, and palm branches, and branches of [?] trees, and make yourselves booths as it is written."

And the people went out and brought them, and each man made himself a booth on his own roof, and each in the court of the house of his God, and in the streets of the city, as far as the gate of Ephraim.

And the whole people of the assembly who had returned from their captivity made booths. And all of them sat in the booths, for the children of Israel had never done this until that day. And there was very great rejoicing.

And he read from the books of the old law day after day, from the first day until the seventh day. They kept the feast for seven days, and on the seventh day he brought it to a close according to the law.
And on the twenty-fourth day of that month the children of Israel gathered and began to fast. They put on sackcloth and poured ashes on their heads.
And the children of Israel separated themselves from all the sons of foreigners, and they sought relief [?] for their sins and for the sins of their fathers.
And they stood in their places, and Ezra read from the books of the law of the Lord God, and all the people worshipped the Lord their God.
And on a high place stood the Levites: Jeshua son of Jozadak, and the sons of Kadmiel, Shecaniah son of Sherebiah, and the sons of Asaniah. And they cried out with a loud voice to the Lord their God.
And the Levites, with Jeshua and Kadmiel, said: "Stand up and praise the Lord our God forever, and from age to age. May the glory of the Lord be praised, and may his praise and glory be exalted."

Ezra began to read aloud and said: You alone are the Lord himself. You made heaven, and the heavens of heavens, and all their order, and the earth and everything that is on it, and the sea and everything that is in it. You give life to all things. The hosts of heaven worship you, and the heavens of heavens praise you.
For you alone are the Lord our God. You chose Abraham and brought him out of the land of the Chaldeans, and you gave him the name Abraham.

You found his heart faithful before you. You made a covenant with him to give the land of the Canaanites, the Hittites, the Perizzites, the Jebusites, the Girgashites and the Amorites to him and to his descendants, and you gave it to them forever. You have kept your words forever, for you are righteous, O Lord God.
You saw the suffering of our fathers in Egypt, and you heard their cry at the Red Sea.

You worked signs for them against Pharaoh in Egypt, against all his servants and against all the people of his land. You knew that they had acted arrogantly against your people. And you made your name great to this very day.
You divided the Red Sea before them, and they passed through the middle of the sea as if on dry land. You sank their enemies and pursuers in the depths, like stones in mighty waters.
By day you led them with a pillar of cloud, and by night with a pillar of fire, which lit up the ways they walked on.
You came down on Mount Sinai and spoke to them from heaven. You gave them the judgments of your righteousness, a true law, and good ordinances and commandments.
You made your holy Sabbaths known to them. You gave them commandments, ordinances and law through your servant Moses.

You gave them bread from heaven for food. You made water flow from the rock and gave them drink. You told them to go in and take possession of the land that you had raised your hand and sworn to give them.
But our fathers themselves became lawless. They grew arrogant, stiffened their necks and did not heed your law.

They did not remember the wonders you had done for them. Instead they stiffened their necks and turned their backs on you, and they wanted to go back there and be slaves there in Egypt again. But you, O Lord our God, are merciful and forgiving and very merciful, O Lord our God, kind Lord, and you did not cast them off completely.
Then they made themselves the molten calf and said: "These are the gods who brought us out of the land of Egypt." And they provoked very great wrath.

But in your great mercy and compassion, O Lord, you did not abandon them or scatter them in the wilderness. You did not take away from them the pillar of cloud that led them by day, or the pillar of fire that lit up the ways they walked on at night.
You gave them your holy and good Spirit so that they would understand your law. You did not withhold manna from their mouths, and you gave them water to drink when they were thirsty.
For forty years you led them through the wilderness. Their clothing did not wear out, and their sandals did not [?] split.
You struck down kings and peoples before them. They divided among themselves the land of Sihon, king of the people of Heshbon, and the land of Og, king of the people of Bashan.
And you multiplied their sons like the stars of heaven. And you brought them into the land that you had promised to their fathers, and they took possession of it.

And you crushed before them the inhabitants of the land of Canaan. And you gave them into their hands, together with their kings and the peoples of that land. And they did to them whatever they wished, according to their will and desire.

And they captured their high and rich cities, and took possession of houses full of every good thing: hewn-out cisterns, laid-out vineyards, olive groves, and every good and fruitful tree, for them to eat and be satisfied. And they ate, and were filled, and grew fat, and lived in luxury among the delights that you had given them.
And they turned away from you and turned back from your law. They killed your prophets, who preached to them to return to you.

They provoked you to great anger. And you gave them into the hands of their oppressors, and these oppressed them greatly. Then, in the time of their distress, they cried out to you, and you heard them from heaven. And in your great mercy you delivered them and brought them out of the hands of their pursuers.

When they had rest, they again did evil before you. And you gave them into the hands of their enemies, and these made them suffer evil. And again they cried out, and you heard them in heaven and delivered them in your great mercy.

And again you set a testimony among them, so that they might return to your law. But they became senseless and arrogant, and did not listen to your law and your commands. Nor did they listen to your commandments, which you commanded them, ordering them to keep your commandments and your words, for the man who does the words of your commands shall live by them. But they turned their backs on you, became stiff-necked, and did not listen to your words.

And you were patient with them and sent prophets by the Holy Spirit to testify against them. Even so they did not listen, and you gave them over to the foreign people in the land, who brought them into great misery.

Yet in your great compassion and mercy you did not destroy them completely or cast them away, nor did you separate them from yourself. For you are mighty and merciful, patient and abundant in mercy, O Lord our God.

And now, our God, mighty and great, Almighty and terrible, you are righteous, our true God. Keep your covenant and your mercy, and look upon the misery and distress of us, of our kings, our princes, our priests, our prophets, our fathers, and your people, which has afflicted us and overpowered us from the time of the kings of Assyria until this day.
But you are righteous in all that you have brought upon us for our sins. You have acted justly, for we have sinned against you,
we, and our kings, our priests, and our fathers. We did not keep your commandment that you gave us. Nor did we pay attention to your law, or to your testimony that you set among us.

And your kingdom, and your many good things that you gave us, and this land that you gave us, broad and wide and rich, which leads to glory: we did not serve you in it. Instead we turned our heart away from your law, O Lord, and you gave us into captivity for our sins.
And behold, today we are in servitude. And this land, which you gave to our fathers so that they might eat its richness and its delights in freedom,

now today foreign kings rule over us and eat it up because of our sins. We have fallen into servitude, O Lord our God. They make us and our cattle serve them, and we pay them tribute in servitude as they please. We are in distress and affliction today because of our sins.

Now, because of all this, we make a covenant and a pledge of faith. We believe it, and we will do it and whatever is written in them. Let us confirm these words in writing and seal it: we, our princes, our Levites and our priests.
And these are the ones who seal this document of faith toward you: Nehemiah son of Hachaliah,
Zedekiah son of Seraiah, and Azariah and Jeremiah,
Pashhur, Amariah, Malchijah,
Hattush, Shebaniah, Malluch,
Emethe, Meremoth, Obadiah,
Daniel, Ginnethon, Baruch,
Meshullam, Abijah, Mijamin,
Maadiah, Bilgai, Shemaiah. All these are priests.
And the Levites: Jeshua son of Hananiah, Binnui of the sons of Henadad, Kadmiel,
and his brothers: Zebiah, Hodiah, Kelita, Pelaiah, Hanan,
Mica, Rehob, Hashabiah,
Zaccur, Sherebiah, Shebaniah,
Hodiah, the sons of Beninu.
The leaders of the people: Parosh, Pahath-moab, Elam, Zattu;
the sons of Bani: Azaiath, Bebai,
Adonijah, Bigvai, Adin,
Ater, Hezekiah, Azzur,
Hodiah, Hashum, Bezai,
Hariph, Anathoth, Nebai,
Magpiash, Meshullam, Hezir,
Meshezabel, Zadok, Jaddua,
Pelatiah, Hanan, Azaniah,
Asia, Hananiah, Hasshub,
Hallohesh, Pilha, Shobek,
Rehum, Hashabnah, Maaseiah,
Ahijah, Hanan, Anan,
Malluch, Harim, Baanah,

and the others, the rest of the people: priests, Levites, gatekeepers, singers, Nethinim (temple servants), and all this our people, who hear the law of the Lord our God. We lay down testimony today before you, O Lord: fathers and mothers, sons and daughters, who together [?] transgressed your law, O our God.

We have confirmed it with an oath today before you: let anyone who does not keep your law be accursed and cursed, the law that you gave us by the hand of your servant Moses. Instead, with all our will we shall keep it and do all the will of the Lord, and his judgments and his commandments.
And we will not give our daughters to a foreign people, and we will not bring the daughters of the gentiles to our sons, ever.
And the people of the land shall not bring merchandise to us on the Sabbath day, and we shall keep every seventh [year] holy.
And we will give as a charitable offering the seventh part of the drachma, year by year, as a tribute to the house of God,

and the bread, the first offering, at the appointed times, the sacrifice of all the feasts of the year and of the Sabbaths and of all the new moons, and for the dedication, and for the holy things, and for sins, which is for the atonement of Israel always.

And we will cast lots for the allotment of the wood, which he sent to the priests and the Levites. And the people shall bring it to the house of the Lord our God and to the houses of our fathers at the appointed times, year by year, as is the rule, for burning on the altar of the offerings of the Lord our God, as it is written in the law of Moses.
And we will give the firstfruits of the produce of our land and the fruit of our trees, year by year, to the house of our God.

And the didrachma for our firstborn children, and the firstborn of our flocks, as it is written in the law of Moses. And we shall bring the firstborn of our cattle and of our [?] to the house of our God, to our priests and Levites, who stand in the service of the Lord God.

And we shall offer the first of the wheat and the fruit of the trees, of the vine and of the olive, to the priests in the treasury house of our God. And the Levites shall go and collect the tithe of our land, all of it together.

And a priest from the sons of Aaron shall be with the Levites when they take the tithes. And from our tithe the Levites shall give a tithe to the high priest in the house of our God, in the place of the treasury, which is in the temple of the Lord.

For it was laid up as treasure and store for the sons of the Levites, the ministers, in the place where the holy vessels are. And let it belong to the priests, the Levites, the gatekeepers and the psalm-singers. Let them never lack their provision from the house of the Lord our God, ever, and let them not abandon the service of the Lord.

And the rulers of the people settled in Jerusalem. And the people cast lots so that one out of every ten, whoever the lot fell on, would settle in Jerusalem, the holy city, and the other nine would stay in their own cities.
And the people blessed these men who set themselves apart and settled in Jerusalem.
These are the rulers of the land, and the priests and the Levites and the Nethinim (temple servants) and the sons of Solomon's servants.

Those who lived in Jerusalem were of the tribe of Judah and of Benjamin. These are from the sons of Judah: Athaiah son of Zechariah, son of Amariah, son of Shephatiah, son of Mahalalel, of the sons of Perez.
And of the sons of Males: the son of Baruch, son of Chazae, son of Uzziah, son of Adaiah, son of Joiarib, son of Zechariah, son of Elon.
And all the sons of Perez who settled in Jerusalem were four hundred and sixty-seven mighty men.
These are the sons of Benjamin: Seon son of Meshullam, son of Joed, son of Pedaiah, son of Kolaiah, son of Maaseiah, son of Ithiel, son of Jeshaiah.
After him: Gabbai and Sallai, nine hundred and twenty-eight.
And Joel son of Zichri was inspector and overseer over them, and Judah son of Hassenuah, who was from the second city.
And of the priests: Did son of Joarib, Jachin,
Seraiah son of Hilkiah, son of Meshullam, son of Zadok, son of Meraioth, son of Ahitub. And their houses were near the temple of the Lord.

And his brothers who did the service of the Lord in the house of the Lord were eight hundred and twenty-two. And Adaiah son of Jeroham, son of Pelaliah, son of Amzi, son of Zechariah, son of Pashhur, son of Malchijah.
And his brothers, rulers among the heads of fathers' houses, two hundred and forty-two; and Maasai son of Azarel;
and his brothers, mighty men, twenty-eight in all; and their workers and overseers: Mekriel, who was one of the great chiefs.
And of the Levites: Shemaiah son of Hasshub, son of Hezron,
and the Nethinim, the sons of Micah: Jobab son of Samu(i) [?],
two hundred and seventy-two.

And the gatekeepers: Akkub, Talmon and their brothers, two hundred and seventy-two. In Jerusalem the Levites: of Azarebon [?], son of Hashabiah, son of Mattaniah, son of Micah, of the sons of Asaph, singers near the house of the Lord our God.
For the king's command concerning them was that they should be there in unceasing service.
And Pethahiah of Mesiah [?], Zabiel, Azariel son of Judah, who held all the administration from the king's hand.
And he had settled on his own estate. And of the sons of Judah, those who settled in Kiriath-arba,
and in Iso [?],
and in Beersheba,
and their inheritance, Lachish and its fields, which Beersheba held [?].
And the sons of Benjamin: in Geba and Michmash.
And the Levites, and a portion of Judah and of Benjamin.
These are the priests and the Levites who came up with Zerubbabel son of Shealtiel and Jeshua son of Jozadak: Seraiah, Jeremiah, Ezra,
Amariah, Malluch, Hattush,
Shecaniah.
These were the chiefs of the priests and their brothers in the days of Jeshua.
And the Levites: Jeshua, Binnui, Kadmiel, Sherebiah, Judah, Mattaniah, and their brothers, who had been appointed for each day.
And Jeshua had a son, Joiakim; Joiakim had Eliashib, and Eliashib had Judah.
And Judah had Jonathan, and Jonathan had Jaddua.
And in the days of Joiakim his brothers were priests and heads of the fathers' houses: Seraiah, Emariah, Hananiah, Jeremiah,
Ezra, Meshullam, Amariah, Jonan,
Malluch,
And the Levites in the days of Jasib [Eliashib]: Joiada, Johanan, Judah, who were counted as heads of the fathers' houses. All these were priests during the reign of King Darius.
And the sons of Levi, heads of the fathers' houses, were recorded in the book of the chronicles of the reckoning of days, up to the days of Jonan son of Jasob.

And the chiefs of the Levites: Hashabiah and Sherebiah, Jeshua and the sons of Kadmiel, and their brothers beside them, blessed and sang praises, as David, the man of God, had commanded, day by day and all the days,
among their people, together with the gatekeepers.
These were in the days of Joiakim son of Jeshua son of Jozadak, in the days of Nehemiah and of Ezra the priest, the scribe of the law of the Lord.

And at the dedication of the wall of Jerusalem they sought out the Levites in their places, to bring them to Jerusalem to hold the dedication with joy and thanksgiving and praise, with instruments [?], cymbals, harps and psalteries, with songs of praise and the sound of the horn trumpet.
All those who praised and sang gathered from around Jerusalem and from the cities,
and from the villages and their homes, to come to Jerusalem for the reverent service.
All the priests and the Levites purified themselves, and they purified the people and the gatekeepers of the great gate of the wall.
And they brought the chiefs of Judah up onto the wall, and followed after them two by two with the praise of instruments.
Hoshaiah and Azariah, half of the chiefs of Judah.
Azariah, Ezra, Meshullam,
Judah, Benjamin and Salmiah, Jeremiah,
From the sons of the priests there were those who blew the trumpet: Zechariah son of Jonathan, son of Shemaiah, son of Mattaniah, son of Micaiah, son of Zaccur, son of Asaph.
And of the brothers: Samariel and Ezriel blessed and praised with the song of David, the man of God, which he had established. And Ezra the scribe went before them at the gates.

And those who praised went opposite him, and went up by the ascent of the city of David and by the ascent of the wall, above the houses of David, as far as the gate of the waters of Ephraim on the east side.
And the Ibuturean [?] gate, and as far as the tower of Ameel, and as far as the gate of the waters that pour down.
And the sound of praise was heard in every place, for Ezra commanded everyone to stand on the gates to praise and glorify the Lord.

And on that day they offered very great sacrifices and rejoiced, for God had made them glad with great joy. Their wives, their sons and their daughters also rejoiced. And the joy of Jerusalem was heard in distant places.

And on that day they appointed men over the treasures of the treasury, the firstfruits and the tithes, which were gathered there together from the rulers of the city, as the law of Moses commanded for the priests and the Levites.
And those who were the singers of psalms and the gatekeepers took care of the holy things of God and kept the holiness of God, as David and his son Solomon had ordained.
For in the days of David, Asaph was leader and chief of the praise and the singing, of those who praised and glorified God with [?].

And in the days of Zerubbabel and in the days of Nehemiah all Israel gave the portion and share to the singers and the gatekeepers. It was set day by day. And they consecrated portions for the Levites, and the Levites consecrated portions for the sons of Aaron.
On that day the book of Moses was read aloud in the hearing of the people, and that day it was found written thus: "No Ammonite or Moabite shall ever enter the assembly of God."
For they did not meet the sons of Israel with bread and water, but hired Balaam the soothsayer to curse them. And God turned the curse into a blessing.
And when they heard the law, they separated and set apart all those who had mixed with Israel.
And before this, Eliashib the priest had given Tobiah a place in the treasury of the house of the Lord our God.

And he made a house for himself, a great treasury, and he stayed there. Before that, they had put there the manna, the frankincense, the vessels of the sanctuary, the tithe of wheat, wine and oil, the rations of the Levites, the singers and the gatekeepers, and the firstfruits of the priests.
And while all this was being done I was not in Jerusalem, for in the thirty-second year of Artaxerxes, king of the Babylonians, I went in before the king. After a long time I asked leave of the king.
And I came to Jerusalem and saw all the wickedness that Eliashib had done for Tobiah, for he had given him the use of the treasury room in the court of the house of the Lord.
And this displeased me greatly, and I threw all of Tobiah's belongings out of the treasury room.
And I gave orders to cleanse the treasury room of the Lord. And I brought the service vessels of the Lord and all the frankincense back into it.
And I saw and learned that the portion of the Levites had not been given, and they had gone away to their own fields. The Levites and the singers were doing the work of their own labor.
And I rebuked the rulers and said, "Why has the ration been withheld from the house of the Lord?" And I gathered all those servants and set them back in their places.
And all the Jews brought the tithe of wheat, wine and oil into the treasury of the house of the Lord.

And I gave orders that it be given into the hands of Shelemiah the priest, Zadok the scribe and Pedaiah, who was one of the Levites. And from their hand [?] Hanan son of Zaccur, son of Mattaniah. They were considered trustworthy, and they were to divide it and give it to all the brethren.
May God remember me in all this, and may he not take his mercy away from me, for I did all this for the house of the Lord God of Israel.

In those days I saw in Judea that they were treading the winepress on the Sabbath and bringing sheaves in through the gates of Jerusalem. And they loaded wine, grapes and figs onto [?]. And they took up heavy burdens and brought them into Jerusalem. And I saw all this on the Sabbath day. I appointed three witnesses, for they were [?] on the Sabbath day
and they sat in the place of those merchants of Judah, who brought in fish to sell, and all kinds of wares and wine and all kinds of merchandise on the Sabbath day to the Jews in Jerusalem.

And I contended with the sons of the Jews who were in Jerusalem and with the rulers of Judah, and I said to them: "What is this lawlessness upon you and upon your children that you are committing? You are profaning the holy Sabbath day and corrupting it."

"Did your fathers not do exactly this? And because of you God brought all this harm and evil on them and on this city of Jerusalem. And now why are you adding to the wrath upon Jerusalem and profaning the Sabbath day?"

And when I had set up the gates of Jerusalem before the Sabbath, I ordered that those gates be shut, and I did not allow them to be opened until the Sabbath had passed. And then I stationed guards so that they would let no one carrying a burden enter the gates of Jerusalem on the Sabbath day.
And all those who traded around Jerusalem lodged outside once and twice.
And I said to them: "Why are you lodging outside the wall? If I see your lawlessness again, you who are still here, I will give orders that you may not come in on our Sabbath or into our city."

And I told the Levites who had been purified to come and guard the gates, and they sanctified the Sabbath day. From then on they did not profane the Sabbath. And in all this the Lord God remembered me and showed me compassion in his abundant mercy.
In those days I saw the Jews, and that Azotian and Ammonite women were living among them,
and that their children, some of them born of those mothers, spoke Azotian and did not know the Jewish language.

And I was angry with them and cursed them. And I beat many of the men among them. And I made all of them swear by the name of God that they would not give their daughters to their sons, nor bring their daughters for their sons. And I said to them:

"Did Solomon king of Israel not sin through all this? And who among all our kings was as wise as he? He was beloved of our God, and God made him king over all Israel. Yet even such a man, beloved of God, wise and a great king, was turned aside and led into sin by the foreign wives."
"Now let me not hear that anyone has done such a great deed and wickedness, sinning against his God and taking a foreign wife."
I heard that, among the sons of Joiada and of Eliashib the high priest, one had a wife who was a daughter of Sanballat. So I separated him and drove him away from me.
May God remember them for what they did to the inheritance and the covenant of the priesthood.
I purified the Levites from all the foreigners. Day by day I put the priests and the Levites in order and made them ready, and I assigned the men each to his own work.

I also ordered them to bring all the wood for the altars carefully and in good order, each at its proper time, as well as the first of their fruits. And now may God remember us in all the good of righteousness.
